tasks.title: Email about pond survey
tasks.instruction:
You must answer this question. Write your answer in about 100 words.

Read this email from your English teacher, Ms. Rivera, and the notes you have made.

Write your email to Ms. Rivera using all the notes.

promptBlocks.text: You must answer this question. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.subject: Pond survey in the city park
paragraphs: As you know, our class is helping with a pond survey in the city park next Saturday. We need to decide on the main goal of the survey. Should we focus on counting the different types of wildlife in the pond, or on testing the water quality to see if it's healthy? Which do you think is more important and why?
Also, we need to choose one practical task for volunteers. Would you prefer to help with setting up equipment near the pond, or with recording the data we collect?
Finally, can you suggest one way to encourage more students to join the survey?

promptBlocks.heading: Notes for your reply
listItems: Say which main goal you prefer and explain why.
Choose a practical task (setting up equipment or recording data) and give a reason.
Suggest one way to encourage more students to join.
Ask Ms. Rivera about the time the survey starts.

promptBlocks.text: Write your email to Ms. Rivera using all the notes.

promptBlocks.text: Answer one of these questions. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.heading: Articles wanted!
paragraphs: A pond survey is happening in our city park next Saturday.
Do you think this survey will help protect urban wildlife?
What is the most interesting thing you would like to learn from the survey?
Write an article answering these questions and we will put it on our website!

designReview.specificSetting: a pond survey in the city park planning brief 10

tasks.scenario: Student replying to English teacher about planning a pond survey in the city park
tasks.purpose: evaluate and justify priorities: choose main goal of survey, choose practical task, suggest encouragement, ask about start time
requiredContentPoints: the main urban wildlife issue (counting wildlife vs. testing water quality)
one practical consequence (setting up equipment or recording data)
a justified recommendation (preferred goal and task)
tasks.originalitySelfCheck: Scenario is specific to pond survey, not generic. Email format with notes panel, four distinct content points. No overlap with existing tests.

tasks.scenario: Writing an article for a local nature website about the pond survey
tasks.purpose: assess effectiveness and recommend: evaluate whether survey helps protect urban wildlife, suggest interesting learning point
requiredContentPoints: the main urban wildlife issue (protection of pond wildlife)
one practical consequence (what can be learned from survey)
a justified recommendation (why survey is useful)
tasks.originalitySelfCheck: Article task uses announcement panel with two direct questions, no reused frame from previous tests. Topic is pond survey, not generic.

tasks.scenario: Writing a story beginning with a specific sentence about the pond survey
tasks.audience: programme coordinator (implicitly, as story audience is English teacher)
tasks.purpose: analyse implications and propose action: story shows how the survey changes the narrator's perspective
requiredContentPoints: the main urban wildlife issue (pond survey)
tasks.originalitySelfCheck: Story opening is unique, not used in any previous test. It directly references the pond survey scenario. No cliché.

designReview.overallOriginalityCheck: All tasks are built around the specific setting 'a pond survey in the city park planning brief 10'. No overlap with any existing test fingerprints. Forbidden concepts avoided. Each task has distinct audience and purpose as per designFingerprint.
